title: Rust session tree navigation and forking
note: Paired clean native builds: base 9a2baf1a835269e8bb8e2a3e03f76e4e2aa86952, candidate 89aa827dee46ae5415476e8127d70dd4d92b6eab. Six standard/extended models, eight standard scenarios, three trials; medium thinking where available and DeepSeek's high default. The slice changes interactive history selection through /tree and /fork. The standard headless suite does not exercise those commands; separate compiled-provider and real-gateway fullscreen/inline scenarios check selected ancestry, draft restoration, excluded history, source-file preservation, fork writes and terminal restoration. No performance claim. The sole flag is GPT tool errors 0 -> 1. In candidate ordinary_edit trial 0, the model sent overlapping edits; the unchanged edit tool rejected them, the model corrected the call, and the task succeeded. This flag is accepted for this opt-in UI/navigation slice as a model-generated invalid call followed by successful recovery: no changed tool implementation or headless input was found. All 144 paired system prompts match after executable/temporary-path normalization; the six captured first-request pairs match except prompt_cache_key for two models. That evidence supports the disposition but does not establish identical generated responses. GPT succeeds in 23/24 candidate and 19/24 baseline samples: candidate ordinary_edit trial 1 and four baseline samples hit the existing trailing-whitespace tool-call guard; baseline multi_file_edit trial 1 hit the 180-second wall-clock limit after one request and no tool call. These failures remain unresolved provider reliability evidence; all samples are retained, with no retry replacement. Every other model passes 24/24 on each arm. DeepSeek Flash has two baseline tool errors from shell discovery and a diagnostic test before successful repair, versus zero candidate tool errors. There are no additional regression flags.

settings.effort: medium where the model offers it; DeepSeek runs at high, its default, having no medium

regressionRule: all tasks, per model: total tokens with the 95% interval above zero; requests up more than 10% with the 95% interval above zero; failures +2 or more; any tool-error increase
